verdicts.reason: Computed from the provider's own claims only; no label or cross-provider information.
Personalised PageRank is seeded on all flagged providers, including validation and test providers, and a provider's own label propagates into its score.
It is multiplied by the provider's label rank, which uses the PotentialFraud label directly. Standardising with test-set statistics adds further leakage.

Flags come only from training-fold providers and each training provider's own fold is excluded, so neither its own label nor held-out labels are used. This holds only if the same out-of-fold scheme is applied inside every CV split and for test scoring.
It is computed over all 5,410 labelled providers, so it includes the provider's own label and the labels of validation and test providers.
Aggregates beneficiary attributes for the provider's own claims; no label or audit information.
An investigation opened after the review period only exists after an audit decision, and it is likely tied to the label.
Per-provider ratio from the provider's own claims; no label involved.
Per-provider ratio from the provider's own claims; no label involved.
Per-provider aggregate of its own inpatient claims; no label involved.
Per-provider ratio from the provider's own claims; no label involved.
Target encoding of the provider's own PotentialFraud label fitted on all providers, so it contains the label and the validation and test labels.

It uses no labels, but it is built from claims of all providers, including test providers. This is unsupervised and usually acceptable, but it is a transductive use of test data. It is fine if the claims-level graph would be available at scoring time.
Computed from the provider's own claims; no label or post-audit information.
Per-provider mean from its own claims; no label involved.

split_comment: A stratified provider-level split with a test set opened once and repeated CV on development is sound, since providers do not straddle folds. Any label-derived or graph features must be refit inside each fold. With about 9.35% positives, the test set has roughly 100 positives, so PR-AUC will be noisy. The undocumented label origin means results measure agreement with suspicion, not confirmed fraud.
